description: A clause of SOURCE-COMPUTER or OBJECT-COMPUTER WITHOUT computer-name-1. ISO 2002 makes computer-name-1 optional before the clauses: §2002:12.2.4.1 prints SOURCE-COMPUTER's WITH DEBUGGING MODE clause in a bracket of its own, and ISO §2023:12.3.6.2 lets the OBJECT-COMPUTER clauses (PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE, CHARACTER CLASSIFICATION) follow the paragraph's period directly. X3.23-1985 hung every clause (WITH DEBUGGING MODE; MEMORY SIZE, PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE, SEGMENT-LIMIT) off a REQUIRED computer-name, so the name-less clause form is a 2002 relaxation; the empty paragraph (and SOURCE-COMPUTER's, §2023:12.3.5.2) was legal at 85 already. Parsed at every edition (superset-parse / bind-narrow) so the below-2002 rejection is this named gate rather than `unexpected 'PROGRAM'`. kb/Work PB78 (OBJECT-COMPUTER), PB5609 (SOURCE-COMPUTER).
display: a SOURCE-COMPUTER or OBJECT-COMPUTER clause without computer-name-1
citation: §2002:12.2.4.1 (SOURCE-COMPUTER: [computer-name-1] [WITH DEBUGGING MODE]) and ISO §2023:12.3.6.2 (OBJECT-COMPUTER: [computer-name-1] before the clause set) — 2002 relaxation of the '85 required-name formats
vcr: 2002 relaxation: computer-name-1 optional in SOURCE-COMPUTER and OBJECT-COMPUTER, and the OBJECT-COMPUTER clauses may stand without it (§2023:12.3.5.2 / §2023:12.3.6.2; the '85 formats required the name before any clause)

IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. CNOPT.
ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
CONFIGURATION SECTION.
OBJECT-COMPUTER.
    PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE IS AL.
SPECIAL-NAMES.
    ALPHABET AL IS STANDARD-1.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 A PIC X VALUE "a".
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN.
    IF A > "B" DISPLAY "GT" ELSE DISPLAY "LE" END-IF.
    STOP RUN.
